system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}

Use of canakinumab in the cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome.

Background The cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome (CAPS) is a rare inherited inflammatory disease associated with overproduction of interleukin-1. Canakinumab is a human anti-interleukin-1beta monoclonal antibody. Methods We performed a three-part, 48-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized withdrawal study of canakinumab in patients with CAPS. In part 1, 35 patients received 150 mg of canakinumab subcutaneously. Those with a complete response to treatment entered part 2 and were randomly assigned to receive either 150 mg of canakinumab or placebo every 8 weeks for up to 24 weeks. After the completion of part 2 or at the time of relapse, whichever occurred first, patients proceeded to part 3 and received at least two more doses of canakinumab. We evaluated therapeutic responses using disease-activity scores and analysis of levels of C-reactive protein (CRP) and serum amyloid A protein (SAA). Results In part 1 of the study, 34 of the 35 patients (97%) had a complete response to canakinumab. Of these patients, 31 entered part 2, and all 15 patients receiving canakinumab remained in remission. Disease flares occurred in 13 of the 16 patients (81%) receiving placebo (P Conclusions Treatment with subcutaneous canakinumab once every 8 weeks was associated with a rapid remission of symptoms in most patients with CAPS. (ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00465985.)
